pr_title: roachtest: add schemachange/leasing-benchmark for session based leasing
pr_body:
This patch adds a new test to confirm the benefits of session based leasing in a multi-region scenario. The simulated scenario is one where the lease manager cannot refresh all descriptors in time with expiry based leasing. This means that once the lease expires we need to reacquire it. This test intentionally selects a large number of descriptors to achieve this. The session based model will not need any reacquisition's, since these do not require a refresh, showing the latency benefits on select queries (on infrequently accessed tables).

We will compare how long the two different settings take selecting these tables multiple times.

The typical improvement we observe is a neighbourhood of 50% faster by avoiding round trips, for example:
```session based leasing produced an improvement of 63% (session based execution time=4m17.25139875s, expiry based execution time=7m1.550555125s)```

Fixes: #119871
Release note: None

issue_context.title: lease: add new benchmark or roachtest to measure leasing improvements
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
With the work of https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/95765 completed, we should measure the impact the change had.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I think the best option is to add a new roachtest that runs with `sql.catalog.experimental_use_session_based_leasing` set to `off` or `session`. The cluster could be a multi-region cluster, since that's where we expect to see the most benefit. The workload setup should create  a lot of descriptors (e.g. more than 500 objects in a single database). The workload should run schema changes while performing DML. (The schema changes themselves can be fairly simple; perhaps just adding/dropping a nullable column on all the various tables.)

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
A unit test benchmark might also be able to reveal the performance improvements.

Epic CRDB-35665

Jira issue: CRDB-36364
